name: gizza-ai/weblog-attack-analyzer
summary: Flag web attack attempts and noisy offenders in access logs

tool.description: Analyze pasted Apache/Nginx or IIS access logs for common web-attack traffic. Flags SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, file inclusion, RCE payloads, scanner user agents (sqlmap, nikto, nuclei, etc.), sensitive-path probes (.env, .git, wp-login, phpMyAdmin), and high-volume / enumeration / brute-force source IPs. Percent-decodes request targets by default to catch encoded payloads. Outputs a report, table, JSON, CSV, or an IP blocklist. Runs locally on pasted log text; it is a heuristic triage aid, not a WAF or IDS replacement.

category.description: Attack category filter: all (default), SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, remote code execution, file inclusion, scanner user agents, or sensitive-path probes.

decode.description: Also scan once- and twice-percent-decoded request targets so encoded payloads are caught. Default true.

error_threshold.description: 404s or 401/403s from one source IP needed to label enumeration or brute-force behaviour (1-100000). Default 5; pass 0 to use the default.

limit.description: Maximum flagged requests to render in report/table/json/csv outputs (1-5000). Default 500; counts always cover the whole log.

logs.description: Apache/Nginx common or combined access-log lines, or IIS W3C extended logs with a #Fields header. Paste one request per line.

min_severity.description: Minimum severity to report. all (default) includes low through critical; high hides low/medium probes; critical shows only critical SQLi/RCE-style findings.

offender_threshold.description: Requests from one source IP needed to label it high-volume (1-100000). Default 20; pass 0 in CLI/chat to use the default.

output.description: Output format: report (default Markdown-style summary), table, json, csv, or blocklist (one offending IP per line).
